english.title: Cause to be published an advertisement to sell / buy dead Schedule 1 wild bird
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person who was not registered for the purpose, caused to be published an advertisement, which was likely to be understood as conveying that you would buy or sell, or intended to buy or sell

(A)_[a dead wild bird]_
(B)_[dead wild birds]_
(C)_[part or parts of or anything derived from a dead wild bird]_
(D)_[parts of or anything derived from dead wild birds]_

included in Schedule 1 to the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981, namely **(..SPECIFY..)
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 6(2)(b), 6(4) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Where more than one bird is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each bird (Section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
